 Formula One 2026 Mexican Formula One Grand Prix: Antonelli becomes youngest F1 champion as Verstappen wins – live
 🏎️ Report: Antonelli wins world championship at age of 20 
 🏎️ Email beau.dure@theguardian.com or chat to him on BlueSky 
 LIVE  Updated  3m ago Beau Dure Sun 1 Nov 2026 17.25 EST First published on Sun 1 Nov 2026 14.00 EST Share Key events 3m ago Kimi Antonelli wins the F1 championship!

 2m ago 17.25 EST Antonelli lifts his visor and wipes tears from his eyes.
 Share 3m ago 17.24 EST Kimi Antonelli wins the F1 championship!
 It’s Verstappen, Hamilton, Antonelli, Leclerc, Norris.
 Share 4m ago 17.24 EST Lap 71 of 71: Hamilton hasn’t had a chance to make a serious run at Verstappen. Norris tries a couple more times to pass Leclerc but can’t.
 Share 5m ago 17.23 EST Lap 70 of 71: Leclerc is now playing Lucy to Norris’ Charlie Brown. Norris gets so close through a few turns, and then Leclerc zooms away when the track is straighter.
 Share 6m ago 17.22 EST Lap 69 of 71: The top three have left Leclerc, Norris and Russell in the dust. Antonelli is surely enjoying these ceremonial laps before he is crowned champion.
 Share 7m ago 17.20 EST Lap 68 of 71: Norris has a go at Leclerc, but the Ferrari is just too fast, tire or no tire.
 Stewards are looking at a Gasly/Lawson incident.
 Brief yellow flag to deal with debris.
 Share 9m ago 17.19 EST Lap 67 of 71: Stewards will take a close look at the Piastri-Lindblad incident after the race.
 Russell is sitting behind the Leclerc-Norris battle, perhaps ready to pounce if they slip up.
 Share 11m ago 17.17 EST Lap 66 of 71: Stewards are looking at the Piastri-Lindbland incident, but that’d be harsh.
 Nothing else has changed. Antonelli is six laps away from the championship.
 Share 12m ago 17.16 EST Lap 65 of 71: Hamilton is still showing no sign of overtaking Verstappen. Leclerc’s tire is literally hanging by a thread, and he’s still ahead of Norris.
 Lawson is up to ninth.
 Share 13m ago 17.14 EST Lap 64 of 71: Verstappen stays ahead of Hamilton. Antonelli has breathing room in third. Leclerc is somehow still ahead of Norris.
 Share 15m ago 17.13 EST Verstappen and Hamilton quickly open space ahead of Antonelli. Leclerc once again has Norris on his tail.
 Share 15m ago 17.12 EST Lap 63 of 71: The safety car’s time comes to an end. Hamilton salivates behind Verstappen …
 Share 16m ago 17.11 EST Lap 62 of 71: Unsung accomplishment of the day: Liam Lawson started on pit road. He’s now in 10th, in the points. That’s quite a drive.
 Leclerc’s tire seems to be in awful shape.
 Share 18m ago 17.09 EST Lap 61 of 71: Piastri asks if he has a little bit of damage or a lot of damage. The team says it’s a “reasonable amount of damage.”
 Share 19m ago 17.08 EST Lap 60 of 71: This crash doesn’t appear to be as serious as the Bottas crash, so a red flag seems unlikely.
 Replay shows Piastri pulled alongside Lindblad, who wound up running over Piastri’s wheel.
 Lindblad’s car has come to rest against the wall without barrier damage, but there’s a bit of debris to clean up.
 Share 22m ago 17.06 EST Lap 59 of 71: Lindblad has hit the wall!
 Yellow flag for now. Then a safety car.
 Lindblad says he’s OK.
 Share 23m ago 17.05 EST Lap 58 of 71: Now both McLarens are trying to pass --= Norris is still behind Leclerc, and Piastri has come up close to Lindblad.
 But Russell is now just behind Norris.
 Norris’ team informs him that Leclerc has a flat spot on his tire. Norris says he already sees it.
 Share 24m ago 17.03 EST Lap 57 of 71: The only scenario now in which Antonelli will not clinch the championship today would be if he has a catastrophic problem while Hamilton passes Verstappen. Or five cars in front of Russell disappearing from the earth.
 Share 25m ago 17.02 EST Lap 56 of 71: Norris is once again right behind a car that he just can’t pass. The Ferraris, for all their costly in-fighting, have been pretty fast, so one would think Leclerc should be able to hold him off, yes?
 Share 27m ago 17.01 EST Lap 55 of 71: Verstappen yells something about the braking. The next time Verstappen complains about the car and then falls off the pace will be the first, as far as I can recall.
 Sainz is under investigation for moving too soon on the restart.
 Share 28m ago 16.59 EST Lap 54 of 71: The gaps are opening up.
 Hamilton is asking his team if they can look into Verstappen bumping into him. The stewards already did. His team doesn’t think he has significant damage.
 Share 30m ago 16.58 EST Lap 52 of 71: Top 10 is Verstappen, Hamilton, Antonelli, Leclerc, Norris, Russell, Lindblad, Piastri, Colapinto, Gasly.
 So the only changes in that bunch from the restart are Hamilton and Antonelli past Leclerc, then Lindblad past Piastri, which is surprising.
 Share 32m ago 16.55 EST Lap 51 of 71: Hamilton posts the fastest lap. Leclerc has complained of vibrations in the tires, and Norris nearly slips past him.
 Hülkenberg gets a 10-second penalty. He’s already back in 16th.
 Verstappen investigation is over, and he’s OK.
 Share 34m ago 16.54 EST Lap 50 of 71: Verstappen noted for being out of position at the restart?? How many twists will this race have?
 Antonelli posts the fastest lap but is still 1.3 seconds behind Hamilton.
 Hülkenberg did indeed make contact with Bearman,.
 Share 35m ago 16.53 EST Lap 49 of 71: Fastest lap goes to Hamilton. There’s no further investigation on the start.
 Farther back – Bearman is out of the race, and Hülkenberg is under investigation for the start. Are those notes related?
 Share 36m ago 16.52 EST Lap 48 of 71: Race control has noted a Hamilton-Verstappen incident, but that can’t be anything.
 Hamilton says he can’t see out of his right mirror.
 For now, they’re comfortably ahead of Antonelli, who is comfortably ahead of Leclerc, who is uncomfortably ahead of Norris.
 Share Updated at  16.53 EST 37m ago 16.50 EST Verstappen is pulling away from Hamilton. Leclerc isn’t thar far back, but Antonelli is closing in on him … and passes!
 Share 38m ago 16.49 EST Restart
 Verstappen goes fast, Hamilton goes behind him and sails into second. Leclerc locks up and kicks up smoke. Verstappen and Hamilton go side by side and barely avoid calamity.
 Hamilton has to be ecstatic at this point.
 View image in fullscreen Max Verstappen leads at the restart. Photograph: Michael Potts/LAT Images Share Updated at  17.03 EST 40m ago 16.48 EST This will be a standing restart. And fraught. Hamilton will be hoping Verstappen flies on the start, giving him room to get past Leclerc.
 Share 47m ago 16.41 EST It’s not a great homecoming for Sergio Perez. His teammate’s car had a catastrophic failure. He’s nearly last among the cars still running.
 And now he’s got a five-second penalty for speeding in the pit lane.
 Less than five minutes before we get rolling again …
 Share 52m ago 16.35 EST Revised standings before the restart
 Want more intrigue? Of course you do!
 The Powers That Be have decreed that the standings for the restart will be based on where they stood before the red flag. 
 Hamilton will therefore move up.
 The resumption order from F1 is, with changes in bold …
 1 Verstappen
 2 Leclerc
 3 Hamilton – up 1
4 Antonelli – down 1
 5 Norris
 6 Russell
 7 Piastri – up 1
8 Lindblad – down 1
 9 Colapinto
 10 Gasly – up 3
11 Hülkenberg – down 1
12 Bearman – down 1
13 Bortoleto – down 1
 14 Hadjar
 15 Lawson
 16 Sainz
 17 Harikawa
 18 Perez – up 1
19 Albon – down 1 
 Race will resume in 10 minutes …
 Share 1h ago 16.22 EST Standings before the restart
 1 Verstappen
 2 Leclerc
 3 Antonelli
 4 Hamilton
 5 Norris
 6 Russell
 7 Lindblad
 8 Piastri
 9 Colapinto
 10 Hülkenberg
 11 Bearman
 12 Bortoleto
 13 Gasly
 14 Hadjar
 One lap down …
 15 Lawson
 16 Sainz
 17 Hirakawa
 18 Albon
 19 Perez
 Out
 Bottas
 Stroll
 Alonso
 Share 1h ago 16.18 EST Ferrari – bad luck or bad strategy? Or bad driving? 
 To recap the day of Lewis Hamilton, who came into the day almost giddy after winning his first pole in three years …
 Leclerc, his teammate, pulled up alongside him and wound up going far off the track. Hamilton also wound up off the track a bit. Leclerc got a five-second penalty but also spent dozens of laps enjoying the clean air of first place.
 With the safety car deployed, Ferrari quickly pulled Hamilton into the pits – but not Leclerc, though maybe he wasn’t in position to pit right away. Hamilton dropped a place to Antonelli.
 Should Ferrari have waited for a possible red flag before bringing in Hamilton? Or is that expecting too much psychic ability of the Ferrari team?
 Share 1h ago 16.11 EST Replay of the Bottas accident from his onboard camera – his left front wheel just suddenly popped up out of place. The car whipped around 180 degrees as it skided toward the barrier.
 Must be terrifying. Nothing he could do but hit the brakes to slow down as much as he could.
 He did walk away from the accident, looking a little worse for wear but also waving to the crowd.
 Share 1h ago 16.09 EST Bottas is out of the car.
 Hamilton on the radio: “We’ve got big problems. Big, big problems.”
 Share 1h ago 16.08 EST Red flag
 Lap 46 of 71: Bottas has given a thumbs-up and seems to be moving OK, but there’s enough damage to car and barrier to put out the red flag.
 Hamilton can only curse his rotten luck. His pit stop has been rendered pointless, and now the world champion-in-waiting is between him and his teammate/arch-enemy Leclerc.
 Share 1h ago 16.07 EST Safety car enters
 Lap 45 of 71: Valtteri Bottas has crashed. We have a safety car, and Hamilton immediately pits to get onto soft tires. Russell follows. Then Piastri.
 And fastest lap now belongs to … Hadjuk?
 Antonelli is informed of the safety car. He responds with a bleeped word. The “stay out forever” strategy has now been dashed.
 View image in fullscreen Valteri Bottas suffers a suspension failure at the Mexico GP. Photograph: Sky Sports Share Updated at  16.15 EST 1h ago 16.05 EST Lap 44 of 71: Antonelli finally pits. The crew has a little bobble, but he returns in fourth, 12.4 seconds behind Hamilton and 6.1 ahead of Norris. This should be easy …
 Or …
 Share 1h ago 16.03 EST Lap 43 of 71: Leclerc says the car is difficult to drive. I’d imagine at least 18 of the other 21 drivers in this race are not the least bit sympathetic.
 Share 1h ago 16.02 EST Lap 42 of 71: Hadjar pits for the second time. The first was likely a result of the messy start.
 Albon also pits, but please don’t ask me to try to explain pit strategy of drivers battling for 15th place.
 Share 1h ago 16.01 EST Lap 41 of 71: Bearman pits – awkwardly. Nearly grazed a wall. He returns in 14th.
 Antonelli is the only driver who has not yet pitted. He might as well wave to the crowd as he zips around the track in first place.
 Share 1h ago 15.59 EST Lap 40 of 71: Bortoleto pits and comes back out in 15th. Norris pits, but he overshoots his space! That’ll cost him some time.
 Antonelli and Bearman are the only drivers yet to pit. If Antonelli pits now, he’d almost surely come out in fourth. Bearman would drop far outside the points.
 Share 2h ago 15.57 EST Lap 39 of 71: OK – standings with pit stops included …
 1 Antonelli, not yet (soft tires)
 2 Norris, not yet (soft)
 3 Verstappen, yes (soft)
 4 Leclerc, yes (medium)
 5 Hamilton, yes (medium)
 6 Russell, yes (medium)
 7 Piastri, yes (medium)
 8 Bearman, no (soft)
 9 Bortoleto, no (medium)
 10 Lindblad, yes (medium)
 Share 2h ago 15.54 EST Lap 38 of 71: We may no longer have such a thing as clean air – the leaders have lapped the Cadillacs and then Hirakawa.
 Share 2h ago 15.54 EST Lap 37 of 71: I’ve been waiting for Antonelli and Norris to pit before updating the standings, but they keep hanging on out there.
 Share 2h ago 15.52 EST Lap 35 of 71: Worth noting – Hamilton posted that fastest lap on the medium tires, not soft.
 Colapinto has pitted, so Piastri, Bearman, Bortoleto, Hadjar and Gasly have gone past. Not sure which of those drivers has pitted.
 Share 2h ago 15.50 EST Lap 34 of 71: Russell is pitting, and he’ll serve his 10-second penalty. He returns to action in eighth place. He’s behind Colapinto, who is quietly having a good run.
 Share 2h ago 15.49 EST Lap 33 of 71: Well, well, well … Hamilton has posted the fastest lap! He’s 2.5 seconds behind his current object of derision, teammate Charles Leclerc.
 Share 2h ago 15.47 EST Lap 32 of 71: How long will the Mercedes pair, running 1-2, stay out on soft tires? Reminder: Russell has to serve a 10-second penalty.
 Perez pits, and there’s a glitch. He’s back out, but he lost a considerable amount of time there. His shot at the points is probably gone.
 Share 2h ago 15.46 EST Lap 31 of 71: Verstappen posts the fastest lap.
 Antonelli leads by 4.3, and then Norris is where he has been – looking tantalizingly at Russell, so close and yet so far.
 I’ll disagree with Hamilton – the stewards haven’t handed Leclerc the race. Ferrari has handed it to Verstappen.
 Share 2h ago 15.44 EST Lap 30 of 71: Verstappen’s team tells him he needs one of his “magic Mexico” races. He’s on soft tires and should be faster than Leclerc, but for how long? When will the soft tires degrade?
 View image in fullscreen Red Bull's Max Verstappen in action during the race. Photograph: Eloisa Sanchez/Reuters Share Updated at  15.50 EST 2h ago 15.43 EST Lap 29 of 71: Will Hamilton get to spend some time out in front in clean air? Nope. Ferrari brings him. Hamilton’s blood pressure must be through the roof.
 Kimi Antonelli leads!! (But he’ll give that back when he pits.)
 Share 2h ago 15.42 EST Lap 28 of 71: Verstappen also pits! The top two drivers are in the pit, but Leclerc must serve the penalty, and Verstappen gets out 1.6 seconds ahead … in fifth, because Hamilton, Antonelli, Russell and Norris have not yet pitted.
 Share 2h ago 15.41 EST Lap 27 of 71: Verstappen pulls with 4.8 seconds. He’s pretty good, you know.
 Piastri pits, and it takes more than 5 seconds instead of the usual 2-point-something.
 Leclerc to the pits!
 Share 2h ago 15.39 EST Lap 26 of 71: Meanwhile, Kimi Antonelli sits contentedly in fourth place, cruising to the F1 championship at age 20. He isn’t challenging Hamilton for third, nor is Russell challenging him from behind.
 View image in fullscreen Mercedes driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli during the Mexican Grand Prix. Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PA Share Updated at  15.52 EST 2h ago 15.38 EST Lap 25 of 71: The lead is 5.1. The intrigue is killing me.
